title: Dual-light photodynamic therapy provides sustained antibacterial effect on biofilm
author: Sakari Nikinmaa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfbcjiiw
materials: Grow the planctonic bacteria and provide a standard bacterial concentration in suspension Grow Streptococcus mutans (ATCC 25175) bacteria for 18 h in an incubator (NuAire DH autoflow 5500, NuAire inc, US), at +36 degrees C, 5% CO 2 in BHI broth (Bio-Rad 3564014, Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc, US).

Grow biofilms in flat-bottom 96-well plates (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc, US) by placing 100 µl of 0.46 OD S. mutans suspension in each well, with 100 µl of BHI-broth growth medium. The well plates must be then incubated in a growth chamber (36°C, 5% CO 2 ). The BHI-broth medium is changed daily to supply fresh growth medium and to wash away the debris. The change of the medium in each well is performed by removing 100 µl of the medium by carefully pipetting and replacing it with a similar amount of fresh BHI broth.

To rule out the sample heating and subsequent effect on bacterial viability, temperature controls are measured (Omega HH41 Digital Thermometer, Omega Engineering, US) in the biofilm wells to confirm temperature levels below 35 degrees during the treatment, with a 100mW/cm 2 radiant flux

After the final light exposure, the entire biofilm from each well is collected and placed into a 1-ml test tube, forming 200 µl of suspension. After meticulous vortexing (Vortex-Genie, Scientific Industries Inc, US), a serial dilution assay ranging from 1:1 to 1:100 000 is performed, using sterile ART filter tips (Thermo Scientific, Waltham, US).

We used live/dead BacLight bacterial viability kit (Molecular Probes. Invitrogen, Eugene, Oregon, USA to stain the bacteria/biofilms. The stains are prepared according to manufacturer directions and must to incubate at room temperature and in the dark for 15 min prior to examination under the confocal scanning laser microscope (CSLM).

For antibacterial effectivity assessment, the 200ul of washed and resuspended ICG incubated bacteria solution can be divided into 5 wells of Nunclon Delta well plates (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc, US) followed by excitation with 810nm NIR LED light. Light intensity was 100mW/cm^2 and the total delivered light dose was 100J/cm^2. Control samples are prepared identically to treated samples excluding the ICG incubation step.

steps.title: Prepare planktonic bacterial suspension
steps.instruction: Grow planktonic bacteria, then dilute the culture with 0.9 % NaCl solution until the optical density reaches 0.46 (measured with a Varian Cary 100 Bio UV‑VIS spectrophotometer and confirmed with a Den 1 McFarland densitometer).

steps.title: Form biofilm in 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Add the OD 0.46 bacterial suspension to each well of a 96‑well plate and incubate under the conditions used for biofilm formation (as described in the original study).

steps.title: Incubate biofilm with ICG
steps.instruction: Remove the growth medium by pipetting and add an equal volume of indocyanine green (ICG) solution (Verdye, Diagnostic Green, GmBH) titrated to 250 µg ml⁻¹. Incubate the plate at room temperature in the dark for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Wash biofilm and set final volume
steps.instruction: Wash the biofilm three times by pipetting away the ICG solution and adding 0.9 % NaCl each time. After the third wash, add 0.9 % NaCl to each well so that the total well volume is 200 µl.

steps.title: Determine LED exposure parameters
steps.instruction: Calculate the required exposure time from the target light energy and the measured irradiance. Irradiance values are obtained with a Thorlabs PM 100D power meter equipped with an S121C sensor and a BTS256 spectroradiometer (Gigahertz‑Optik).

steps.title: Expose biofilm to LED light
steps.instruction: Using custom‑made LED sources (Lumichip Oy), illuminate the wells according to the experimental condition:

substeps.instruction: 810‑nm only: 100 mW cm⁻² irradiance, 100 J cm⁻² energy.
405‑nm only: 80 mW cm⁻² irradiance, 100 J cm⁻² energy.
Dual 405 + 810 nm: 50 mW cm⁻² each, 50 J cm⁻² each.
1:1 ratio (aBL:aPDT): 70 mW cm⁻² each, 50 J cm⁻² each.
3:1 ratio (aBL:aPDT): 130 mW cm⁻² (405 nm) and 40 mW cm⁻² (810 nm), delivering 75 J cm⁻² and 25 J cm⁻² respectively.
1:3 ratio (aBL:aPDT): 40 mW cm⁻² (405 nm) and 130 mW cm⁻² (810 nm), delivering 25 J cm⁻² and 75 J cm⁻² respectively.

steps.title: Replace NaCl with BHI broth
steps.instruction: After illumination, remove the 0.9 % NaCl solution and add an equal volume of BHI broth. Place the plate in an incubator (or proceed directly to CFU counting if this was the final step).

steps.title: Plate biofilm dilutions for CFU counting
steps.instruction: Take 100 µl of each biofilm dilution and spread evenly over a BHI agar plate using a sterile L‑shaped rod.

substeps.instruction: For treated samples, perform serial dilutions from 1:1 to 1:10⁴.
For control samples, perform serial dilutions from 10⁵ to 10⁶.
Select the dilution that yields 30–800 colonies for reliable counting.

steps.title: Incubate agar plates
steps.instruction: Place the inoculated agar plates in an incubator set to 5 % CO₂ and grow for 48 hours.

steps.title: Photograph plates
steps.instruction: After incubation, photograph each plate with a Canon D5 DSLR equipped with a Canon EF 24‑70 mm f/4L lens on an Artgraph Light Pad Revolution 80, capturing the entire plate surface.

steps.title: Count colonies with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Import the plate photographs into Image J software (NIH) and count the CFUs.

steps.title: Image biofilm by confocal microscopy
steps.instruction: Examine the biofilm structure using a Leica TCS CARS SP 8X confocal microscope with HC PL APO CS2 20×/0.75 multi‑immersion and HX PL APO CS2 63×/1.2 water‑immersion objectives.

steps.title: Configure confocal laser windows
steps.instruction: Set the emission window for the 488‑nm Argon laser to 500‑530 nm and for the 561‑nm DPSS laser to 620‑640 nm, ensuring exclusion of the excitation wavelengths and compatibility with the live/dead fluorescence marker.

steps.title: Prepare S. mutans pellet for ICG binding
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml of S. mutans suspension (OD 0.46, ≈1 × 10⁸ CFU) to a 2‑ml Eppendorf tube and centrifuge for 5 minutes at 8000 rpm (Heraeus Megafuge 1.0) to obtain a ~10 µl pellet.

steps.title: Bind ICG to bacterial pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and add 1 mg ml⁻¹ ICG solution to bring the total volume to 1 ml. Vortex for 60 seconds, then incubate in the dark for 10 minutes. Wash twice by centrifugation, resuspending the pellet each time in 0.9 % NaCl, and finally centrifuge at 8000 rpm for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Perform absorption spectroscopy
steps.instruction: Vortex the ICG‑bound pellet into fresh 0.9 % NaCl to obtain an OD 0.46 suspension and measure its absorbance with a Varian Gary 100 Bio UV‑visible spectrophotometer. Use a 4 µg ml⁻¹ ICG in 0.9 % NaCl solution as the ICG reference and 0.9 % NaCl alone as the blank.
